residual_or_irreversible_elements: Lost versions, erased practices, prior exposure, assimilation, and historical exclusions may not be restored.
prerequisites: Preserved versions, plural stewardship, affected-party participation, resources, and fresh authority.

explicit_non_implications: A shared story artifact is not shared belief, collective mind, truth, legitimacy, authority, causal influence, or destiny.

required_for: Publishing, teaching, translating, stewarding, restricting, or effectfully using a story artifact.
non_implications: Stewardship, survival, sacred status, popularity, or institutional selection does not itself grant authority over the artifact or community.

candidate_mediators: Which exposures, interpretations, relationships, institutions, incentives, and material practices could connect the artifact to a later observation?
alternative_causes: Which shared conditions, earlier practices, selection processes, or later reinterpretations could account for apparent continuity or change?
non_implications: Artifact survival, recurrence, or institutional use establishes no belief, persuasion, behavior, or civilisational effect.

stages.label: Circulation, exposure, and response
stages.definition: Distribution, availability, measured exposure or attention proxy, and attributed public response remain separately evidenced events rather than a single uptake step.

carriers: Publishers, platforms, broadcasters, gatherings, schools, libraries, networks, search indexes, recommendations, and interpersonal relays.
transformations: Selection, ranking, repetition, moderation, segmentation, translation, summarization, commentary, and measurement operationalization.
gates: Publication rights, audience and privacy boundaries, channel access, measurement validity, non-targeting, and response attribution.

temporal_profile.onset: Availability, delivery, exposure proxy, attention proxy, and response each have distinct possible onset times.
temporal_profile.duration: Channel availability does not specify exposure or response duration.
temporal_profile.latency: Delay among distribution, possible exposure, public response, and record creation is unknown unless measured.
temporal_profile.overlap: Channels, campaigns, organic sharing, counterstory, and external events may overlap.
temporal_profile.decay: Visibility, recall proxies, access, and response traces may decay at different rates.
temporal_profile.recurrence: Redistribution, resurfacing, repetition, and renewed response may recur.
temporal_profile.censoring: Private exposure, avoidance, deletion, moderation, nonresponse, and inaccessible channels censor observation.
temporal_profile.resolution: Declare channel, population, construct, window, sampling, and timestamp resolution separately.

inflows: Published instances, delivery witnesses, scoped exposure measurements, and attributed public responses.
outflows: Deletion, expiration, channel loss, access withdrawal, measurement invalidation, or deduplication.
decay_or_reset: Window expiry, construct change, instrument drift, platform change, or declared cohort reset.
accumulation_profile.scope: One declared artifact-channel-population-window-instrument combination; incompatible measures are not combined.

observables: Channel and surface, availability or delivery witness, sampling and instrument, privacy boundary, response artifact, attribution, timestamp, deletion, and counterevidence.

benefits: Access, discoverability, public reply, and coordination opportunity may be unevenly distributed.
burdens: Exposure, moderation, attention labor, surveillance, bandwidth, and response costs may fall on different parties.
risks: Unwanted exposure, harassment, exclusion, surveillance, manipulation, chilling, and displacement beyond measured channels.
voice_and_options: Keep avoidance, anonymity, refusal, correction, appeal, opt-out, alternative channel, and nonresponse visible.
horizons: Immediate visibility, delayed resurfacing, archival discoverability, and cumulative platform change require distinct windows.

translation_profile.source_language: Declared source language or sign system; unknown until source-bound evidence is added.
translation_profile.target_language: Declared target language or sign system; unknown until source-bound evidence is added.
translation_profile.source_register: Declared source register and institutional setting; unknown until evidenced.
translation_profile.target_register: Declared target register and institutional setting; unknown until evidenced.
translation_profile.source_genre: Declared source genre; unknown until evidenced.
translation_profile.target_genre: Declared target genre; unknown until evidenced.
translation_profile.source_version: Stable source version or witnessed performance reference; none is added by this atlas.

distortions: Ranking, moderation, bot activity, repeated delivery, proxy drift, survivorship, selection, and platform incentives can distort exposure and response records.
counterflows: Avoidance, refusal, blocking, counterstory, correction, alternative channel, contextual reply, moderation appeal, and privacy-preserving nonresponse.
failure_modes: Availability becomes exposure, exposure proxy becomes attention, attention becomes belief, response becomes population opinion, or silence becomes consent.
repair_routes: Correct attribution and measurement, disclose coverage, stop harmful distribution, preserve evidence, restore reply or appeal, and assess displaced effects.
repair_residuals: Copied artifacts, remembered exposure, harassment, chilling, data retention, and off-platform displacement may remain.
repair_recurrence_checks: Review resurfacing, substitute channels, ranking drift, repeated exposure, retaliation, and measurement exclusion under a fresh window.
evidence_requirements: Artifact version, channel, surface, opportunity set, instrument, population, selection process, timestamps, privacy controls, response attribution, negative cases, and missingness.
alternative_paths: Independent discovery, interpersonal relay, common external event, prior belief, institutional cue, avoidance, or substitute channel may explain later traces.
stop_conditions: Stop distribution or measurement when rights, privacy, safety, lawful basis, construct validity, or anti-targeting boundaries fail.
stall_or_block_conditions: Channel denial, censorship, access cost, language barrier, device or infrastructure failure, avoidance, exclusion, moderation, or inadequate sampling.

recoverable_elements: Current availability, ranking, access, measurement, attribution, and reply routes may be changed.
residual_or_irreversible_elements: Prior exposure, copying, data capture, harassment, chilling, and displaced circulation may persist.
prerequisites: Channel control, evidence preservation, affected-party review, privacy protection, and fresh authorization.

explicit_non_implications: Distribution is not exposure; exposure is not attention; attention is not belief; response is not representativeness, consent, persuasion, or effect.

required_for: Publishing, distributing, ranking, measuring, moderating, or contacting any audience.
non_implications: Channel access, a public artifact, or an analytics record grants no authority to expose, target, infer, or act on anyone.

candidate_mediators: Which actual exposures, interpretations, social relays, incentives, or institutional responses could mediate a declared outcome?
alternative_causes: Which prior preferences, shared events, platform changes, selection processes, or measurement artifacts could produce the observed pattern?
non_implications: Temporal ordering, reach, engagement, co-variation, or public response establishes no causal media effect.

stages.label: Institutional selection context
stages.definition: A bounded context of roles, rules, offices, routines, archives, curricula, agendas, non-decisions, exclusions, resources, and inherited constraints through which artifacts or issues may become selectable.

carriers: Organizations, offices, procedures, archives, curricula, budgets, professional roles, infrastructures, customs, and informal networks.
transformations: Admission, credentialing, canon selection, agenda setting, procedural framing, classification, delay, exclusion, routinization, and resource allocation.
gates: Jurisdiction, membership, standing, agenda access, conflict rules, procedural review, public reason, records access, and appeal.

temporal_profile.onset: Institutional forms may have multiple founding, legal, customary, and operational dates.
temporal_profile.duration: Rules, offices, practices, and resource dependencies persist on different horizons.
temporal_profile.latency: Selection effects and non-decisions may become visible only after queues, reviews, or delayed records.
temporal_profile.overlap: Formal and informal institutions, jurisdictions, factions, and inherited practices may overlap.
temporal_profile.decay: Capacity, legitimacy claims, memory, expertise, and compliance may decay differently.
temporal_profile.recurrence: Agenda cycles, ceremonies, elections, reviews, appointments, and crises may recur.
temporal_profile.censoring: Informal vetoes, private deliberations, destroyed records, and excluded parties may be inaccessible.
temporal_profile.resolution: Declare institution, office, rule, population, jurisdiction, practice, and observation window separately.

accumulation_profile.quantity_kind: Institutional memory, rule, resource, and constraint configuration
inflows: Rules, precedents, staff practice, archives, resources, standards, obligations, and learned routines.
outflows: Retirement, repeal, staff loss, budget loss, declassification, decay, exit, and institutional replacement.
decay_or_reset: Review, reform, sunset, jurisdiction change, turnover, crisis, or explicit institutional reset.
accumulation_profile.scope: One named institutional context and jurisdiction over a declared period; forms are not combined into a power total.

observables: Charters, rules, roles, minutes, agendas, queues, budgets, curricula, archives, non-decisions, exclusions, dissent, appeals, and operational practice.

benefits: Standing, access, predictability, resources, recognition, and remedy may be unevenly allocated.
burdens: Compliance, waiting, labor, documentation, exclusion, and adaptation costs may fall elsewhere.
risks: Agenda closure, capture, path lock-in, hierarchy, arbitrary exclusion, coercion, and off-record displacement.
voice_and_options: Track proposal access, dissent, refusal, appeal, exit, representation, alternative institutions, and safe challenge.
horizons: Founding, routine operation, crisis, reform, succession, sunset, and intergenerational obligations require separate review.

distortions: Formal records can hide informal agenda power, non-decisions, unpaid labor, patronage, censorship, coercion, and jurisdictional spillovers.
counterflows: Dissent, opposition, whistleblowing, refusal, appeal, exit, alternate institution, counterarchive, reform, sunset, and external review.
failure_modes: Institutional form is treated as stasis, procedure as legitimacy, office as authority, persistence as effectiveness, or formal equality as equal power.
repair_routes: Open records and agenda review, restore standing and appeal, correct exclusions, resource independent oversight, preserve history, and examine alternatives.
repair_residuals: Lost opportunity, accumulated advantage, stigma, debt, weakened capacity, distrust, and path-dependent obligations may remain.
repair_recurrence_checks: Test whether informal veto, exclusion, capture, retaliation, unequal waiting, or displaced burden returns after formal reform.
evidence_requirements: Institution-specific rules, roles, jurisdictions, budgets, agendas, non-decisions, practice, dissent, affected parties, exclusions, and comparative alternatives.
alternative_paths: Informal networks, markets, households, movements, rival jurisdictions, professional norms, or non-action may bypass or reshape formal selection.
stop_conditions: Stop an effectful institutional use when jurisdiction, rights, standing, conflict, affected-party review, appeal, or safe challenge is unresolved.
stall_or_block_conditions: Agenda denial, resource scarcity, status barrier, veto, censorship, queue, jurisdiction conflict, fear of retaliation, or absent capability.

recoverable_elements: Rules, offices, access, budgets, records, procedures, and current allocations may be revised.
residual_or_irreversible_elements: Lost time, entrenched advantage, damaged trust, dispossession, ecological harm, and foreclosed options may persist.
prerequisites: Current authority, rights review, affected-party participation, resources, record preservation, and non-retaliation safeguards.

explicit_non_implications: An institution is not static, unitary, legitimate, sovereign, effective, consensual, or causally produced by a story.

required_for: Any institutional decision, rule, allocation, exclusion, coercion, publication, or execution.
non_implications: Institutional existence, office, tradition, procedure, capacity, or public recognition does not establish authentic authority or legitimacy.

candidate_mediators: Which rules, incentives, resources, roles, information channels, sanctions, expectations, or material dependencies could mediate a declared change?
alternative_causes: Which external shocks, coalitions, fiscal conditions, technologies, coercive capacities, or shared histories could explain institutional selection or persistence?
non_implications: Institutional sequence, survival, reform, or co-variation establishes no effect of a prior story or expression.

stages.label: Action proposal
stages.definition: A bounded possible action states purpose, target or subject, scope, alternatives, affected parties, resources, risks, stop path, and repair preview without becoming a decision, authorization, capability, attempt, or execution.

carriers: Proposal document, agenda item, design, petition, bill, budget request, implementation plan, dissent, alternative, or non-action option.
transformations: Problem framing, target definition, option generation, bundling, scoping, cost estimation, risk allocation, and revision.
gates: Attribution, reviewed proposal, affected-party register, rights assessment, alternatives, budget horizon, stop route, and repair readiness.

temporal_profile.onset: Proposal formation, submission, publication, and eligibility may occur at different times.
temporal_profile.duration: Validity, review window, expiry, and implementation horizon must be declared.
temporal_profile.latency: Submission-to-review and review-to-decision delay may be material and unequal.
temporal_profile.overlap: Competing proposals, linked decisions, external shocks, and prior commitments may overlap.
temporal_profile.decay: Evidence, costs, authority assumptions, capability, and affected-party conditions may become stale.
temporal_profile.recurrence: Rejected, deferred, revised, or recurring proposals require new context and gates.
temporal_profile.censoring: Unsubmitted, excluded, confidential, unsafe, or off-agenda alternatives may be missing.
temporal_profile.resolution: Version proposals, amendments, alternatives, affected-party registers, and review dates separately.

accumulation_profile.quantity_kind: Proposal versions, commitments, and declared resource requirements
inflows: New options, evidence, amendments, resources, affected-party input, and risk findings.
outflows: Withdrawal, rejection, expiry, supersession, removed scope, or invalidated evidence.
decay_or_reset: Material change, horizon expiry, changed jurisdiction, fresh review, or proposal retirement.
accumulation_profile.scope: One proposal version and named alternatives under a declared procedure and horizon.

observables: Version, purpose, scope, target or subject, alternatives, reasons, sponsors, costs, risks, affected parties, rights review, stop path, expiry, and dissent.

benefits: Expected benefits must remain party- and horizon-specific rather than netted.
burdens: Cost, labor, compliance, surveillance, opportunity loss, maintenance, and repair obligations must be separately allocated.
risks: Rights intrusion, exclusion, coercion, ecological impact, lock-in, data harm, failure, and burden displacement.
voice_and_options: Record standing, representation limits, dissent, refusal, appeal, alternatives, non-action, and safe exit.
horizons: Pre-decision, implementation, operation, maintenance, exit, repair, and future-party horizons remain distinct.

distortions: Problem framing, urgency, cost omission, strategic bundling, proxy metrics, selective evidence, hidden dependencies, and narrow boundaries can bias review.
counterflows: Counterproposal, amendment, objection, refusal, rights challenge, unbundling, delay, withdrawal, non-action, and alternate institution.
failure_modes: A proposal is treated as a decision, urgency as necessity, predicted benefit as evidence, feasibility as permission, or non-objection as consent.
repair_routes: Withdraw or revise the proposal, broaden affected-party review, restore alternatives, update evidence and costs, preserve dissent, and reopen gates.
repair_residuals: Agenda displacement, participation cost, disclosure, chilling, sunk effort, and early commitment effects may remain.
repair_recurrence_checks: Check repeated framing, omitted parties, stale evidence, scope creep, hidden cost, and reintroduced rejected provisions.
evidence_requirements: Versioned proposal, procedure, purpose, scope, alternatives including non-action, affected-party register, rights and distribution review, resources, uncertainty, stop conditions, and repair plan.
alternative_paths: Revise, split, pilot only under separate authority, use a less intrusive institution, delay for evidence, preserve status quo, or take documented non-action.
stop_conditions: Stop advancement when purpose, rights, affected parties, alternatives, jurisdiction, material feasibility, safety, or repair cannot be responsibly bounded.
stall_or_block_conditions: Agenda exclusion, resource gap, conflict, rights objection, missing evidence, unsafe participation, jurisdiction dispute, or expired conditions.

recoverable_elements: Scope, text, alternatives, budget, schedule, and current review status may be revised or withdrawn.
residual_or_irreversible_elements: Disclosure, agenda displacement, participation burdens, sunk costs, and expectation effects may persist.
prerequisites: Version history, withdrawal path, affected-party review, fresh evidence, and renewed procedure.

explicit_non_implications: A proposal is not a decision, authority, consent, capability, attempt, execution, causal finding, or mandate.

required_for: Advancing, approving, funding, piloting, implementing, or communicating a proposal as institutional policy.
non_implications: Authorship, sponsorship, expertise, public support, a decision, or technical merit does not itself grant authority to act.

candidate_mediators: Which implementation, uptake, resource, behavioral, institutional, or environmental processes would connect the proposed action to a declared outcome?
alternative_causes: Which external trends, selection effects, concurrent policies, prior commitments, or measurement changes could produce that outcome?
non_implications: A theory, rationale, model, forecast, or proposal sequence establishes no causal effect.

stages.label: Decision record
stages.definition: A named process records selection, rejection, deferral, conditioning, or retirement of a proposal with reasons, dissent, scope, date, expiry, and appeal, without itself establishing authority, legitimacy, consent, capability, or execution.

carriers: Vote, order, minute, judgment, resolution, administrative record, delegated choice, veto, deferral, condition, or retirement notice.
transformations: Agenda selection, amendment, bundling, reason-giving, voting, delegation, veto, conditioning, deferral, publication, and appeal.
gates: Decision procedure, current membership and conflicts, proposal identity, quorum or equivalent rule, reasons, dissent, expiry, notice, and appeal.

temporal_profile.onset: Deliberation, formal choice, recording, notice, and effective date may differ.
temporal_profile.duration: Decision validity, conditions, sunset, appeal, and review horizons must be declared.
temporal_profile.latency: Queue, deliberation, publication, appeal, and downstream gate delay may be unequal.
temporal_profile.overlap: Concurrent decisions, jurisdictions, amendments, stays, and external events may overlap.
temporal_profile.decay: Facts, authority claims, membership, capability, and reasons may become stale.
temporal_profile.recurrence: Renewal, reconsideration, appeal, review, and supersession may recur.
temporal_profile.censoring: Private deliberation, informal veto, absent minutes, dissent suppression, and non-decision may be missing.
temporal_profile.resolution: Version proposal, agenda, deliberation, decision, notice, appeal, and effective state separately.

inflows: Selections, conditions, reasons, amendments, dissents, delegated tasks, and review obligations.
outflows: Rejection, expiry, revocation, supersession, fulfillment, stay, or retirement.
decay_or_reset: Sunset, appeal outcome, jurisdiction change, material fact change, or formal reconsideration.
accumulation_profile.scope: One named decision procedure, proposal version, jurisdiction, and validity period.

observables: Proposal version, agenda, decision maker, procedure, participation, conflicts, choice state, reasons, dissent, conditions, date, notice, expiry, appeal, and supersession.

benefits: Recognition, resource priority, procedural clarity, and option creation may favor different parties.
burdens: Delay, compliance, exclusion, lost alternatives, future obligation, and appeal cost may be unequally imposed.
risks: Agenda capture, formalism, conflict, authority laundering, path lock-in, retaliation, and decision-subject erasure.
voice_and_options: Record standing, attendance, representation, dissent, veto, recusal, appeal, exit, review, and non-action distinctly.
horizons: Agenda, choice, notice, effective period, appeal, renewal, sunset, and aftermath need separate horizons.

distortions: Agenda control, bundling, procedural opacity, strategic delay, incomplete records, vote aggregation, conflict, and performative reason-giving can distort the visible choice.
counterflows: Dissent, recusal, veto, amendment, deferral, appeal, stay, judicial or external review, withdrawal, supersession, and non-action.
failure_modes: Decision becomes authority, majority becomes legitimacy, silence becomes consent, procedure becomes justice, or selection becomes implementation.
repair_routes: Stay or revoke the decision, correct the record, restore standing and appeal, separate bundled questions, disclose conflict, and conduct fresh review.
repair_residuals: Lost time, disclosure, exclusion, commitment, distrust, sunk cost, and option foreclosure may remain.
repair_recurrence_checks: Review repeated agenda exclusion, conflict, rubber-stamping, retaliation, stale reasons, scope creep, and bypass of appeal.
evidence_requirements: Exact proposal, named procedure and decision maker, jurisdiction claim, agenda, participants, conflicts, reasons, dissent, conditions, date, notice, expiry, appeal, and current status.
alternative_paths: Reject, defer, condition, split, return for evidence, choose an alternative, preserve non-action, escalate to a different authorized forum, or retire.
stop_conditions: Stop downstream use when procedure, conflict, notice, dissent, current status, appeal, jurisdiction, or affected-party review is unresolved.
stall_or_block_conditions: No quorum or equivalent standing, veto, recusal, missing record, jurisdiction dispute, appeal, stay, resource gap, or unsafe participation.

recoverable_elements: A current decision may be stayed, corrected, revoked, superseded, appealed, or retired.
residual_or_irreversible_elements: Disclosure, lost opportunity, reliance, commitment, status effects, and actions already taken may persist.
prerequisites: Current procedure and authority, notice, preserved record, affected-party participation, and a viable appeal or revocation route.

explicit_non_implications: A decision is not authority, consent, lawful basis, capability, execution, legitimacy, goodness, justice, or causal effect.

required_for: Giving a decision external force, allocating resources, binding a subject, invoking capability, or executing an action.
non_implications: A procedurally valid-looking decision record does not authenticate the principal, jurisdiction, scope, lawful basis, consent, legitimacy, or authority to act.

candidate_mediators: Which notices, incentives, sanctions, resource allocations, operator choices, implementation steps, or expectations could connect a decision to later behavior or outcomes?
alternative_causes: Which concurrent events, preexisting trends, informal practices, independent actors, or anticipated decisions could explain later changes?
non_implications: Selection, publication, or temporal precedence establishes no implementation or causal decision effect.

stages.label: Authorization, rights, and affected-party gate
stages.definition: Current authority and jurisdiction claims, affected-party scope, rights assessment, and each required consent or distinct lawful basis are externally verified for the exact proposed act, purpose, party, and horizon.

carriers: Authority source, delegation, jurisdiction record, affected-party register, rights assessment, consent record, lawful-basis claim, expiry, revocation, and dissent.
transformations: Authentication, scope interpretation, delegation, conflict review, party registration, rights balancing, consent validation, condition setting, expiry, and revocation.
gates: Current principal and issuer, grantee, exact act, target or subject, purpose, jurisdiction, expiry, revocation, rights, affected parties, consent or lawful basis, and appeal.

temporal_profile.onset: Grant, consent, lawful basis, notice, and proposed act may begin at different times.
temporal_profile.duration: Each authorization element has its own validity, purpose, jurisdiction, and retention horizon.
temporal_profile.latency: Verification, notice, withdrawal, revocation, appeal, and propagation delays must be visible.
temporal_profile.overlap: Multiple principals, jurisdictions, rights, consents, lawful bases, and conflicts may overlap.
temporal_profile.decay: Authority, consent, factual predicates, representation, and affected-party scope may expire or change.
temporal_profile.recurrence: Renewal, re-consent, reauthorization, review, challenge, withdrawal, and revocation may recur.
temporal_profile.censoring: Private authority sources, unregistered parties, inaccessible remedies, and unsafe refusal may be missing.

accumulation_profile.quantity_kind: Distinct scoped authorization, rights, consent, and lawful-basis records
inflows: Verified grants, registrations, assessments, consents, lawful-basis claims, conditions, and notices.
outflows: Expiry, withdrawal, revocation, invalidation, supersession, purpose change, or jurisdiction loss.
decay_or_reset: Material change, changed party scope, changed purpose, new rights finding, revocation, or fresh verification.
accumulation_profile.scope: Exact proposed act and affected-party relation; separate grants and bases are never collapsed into a legitimacy score.

observables: Authentic source, principal, issuer, grantee, act, subject, purpose, jurisdiction, scope, conditions, expiry, revocation, affected parties, rights analysis, consent or lawful basis, notice, and appeal.

benefits: Protection, representation, remedy, service, and decisional agency may be unevenly available.
burdens: Consent labor, documentation, exclusion, compliance, surveillance, appeal, and proof burdens may be shifted.
risks: Authority laundering, coerced or invalid consent, jurisdiction overreach, omitted parties, rights tradeoff concealment, and inaccessible remedy.
voice_and_options: Keep refusal, withdrawal, representation limits, dissent, appeal, accommodation, alternative basis, and non-action visible.
horizons: Grant, notice, consent, act, retention, downstream use, review, expiry, revocation, repair, and future-party horizons differ.

distortions: Boilerplate, bundled consent, inaccessible procedure, power dependence, proxy representation, stale authority, jurisdiction ambiguity, and omitted non-users can create false clearance.
counterflows: Refusal, withdrawal, revocation, rights challenge, jurisdiction objection, appeal, accommodation, narrower scope, alternative lawful basis, and non-action.
failure_modes: Decision becomes authority, authority claim becomes authentic authority, signature becomes valid consent, lawful basis becomes legitimacy, or capability becomes permission.
repair_routes: Pause the act, preserve records, notify parties, restore withdrawal and appeal, narrow scope, reverify authority, reassess rights, and make remedy accessible.
repair_residuals: Prior disclosure, coercive pressure, retaliation, lost opportunity, dignity harm, data persistence, and distrust may remain.
repair_recurrence_checks: Review stale grants, scope creep, repeated coercion, invalid consent patterns, omitted parties, retaliation, and inaccessible remedy.
evidence_requirements: Authentic current authority source, exact scope and jurisdiction, conflicts, expiry and revocation, affected-party register, rights assessment, each consent or lawful basis, notice, alternatives, and appeal.
alternative_paths: Narrow or redesign the act, change forum, seek fresh consent, use a separately justified less intrusive basis, provide accommodation, defer, or take non-action.
stop_conditions: Stop before capability or attempt when authority, jurisdiction, rights, party scope, consent or lawful basis, notice, expiry, revocation, or remedy is unresolved.
stall_or_block_conditions: Invalid or expired grant, jurisdiction conflict, refusal, withdrawal, rights conflict, omitted party, unsafe consent, inaccessible process, or stayed decision.

recoverable_elements: A future act can be stopped, scope narrowed, grant revoked, consent withdrawn, record corrected, and remedy opened.
residual_or_irreversible_elements: Prior coercion, disclosure, exclusion, dignity injury, lost time, and third-party propagation may persist.
prerequisites: Immediate stop route, authentic current authority, affected-party notice, preserved evidence, independent review, and resourced remedy.

explicit_non_implications: A verified authority claim is not consent, lawful basis, capability, legitimacy, goodness, proportionality, execution, or causal effect.

required_for: Every effectful invocation or action and every use of protected resources, data, bodies, property, jurisdiction, or coercive capacity.
non_implications: This atlas neither verifies nor grants authority, jurisdiction, rights clearance, consent, lawful basis, legitimacy, or permission.

candidate_mediators: Which sanctions, incentives, trust relations, information, resource controls, operator choices, or material constraints could connect an authorization state to later events?
alternative_causes: Which independent legal duties, social norms, coercion, resource dependence, prior commitments, or external events could explain compliance or noncompliance?
non_implications: Authorization status, consent, lawful basis, or refusal establishes no causal effect, effectiveness, legitimacy, or value.

stages.label: Capability and resources
stages.definition: Technical, human, financial, material, informational, maintenance, safety, and repair capability is evidenced for a bounded action without importing permission, authority, desirability, or predicted success.

carriers: People, skills, care, funds, credit, land, energy, materials, data, software, equipment, facilities, networks, logistics, suppliers, and maintenance systems.
transformations: Procurement, training, hiring, allocation, credentialing, configuration, integration, testing, scheduling, maintenance, and contingency planning.
gates: Current authorization, capability evidence, budget and horizon, safety, labor conditions, supply chain, ecological limits, stop route, and repair readiness.

temporal_profile.onset: Procurement, staffing, access, readiness, and authorization may start at different times.
temporal_profile.duration: Capacity, credentials, funding, supplies, maintenance, and authority expire on separate horizons.
temporal_profile.latency: Acquisition, training, delivery, integration, testing, and repair latency may be substantial.
temporal_profile.overlap: Shared infrastructure, competing demands, outages, seasonal constraints, and supplier dependencies may overlap.
temporal_profile.decay: Skills, software, equipment, funding, materials, data quality, and institutional knowledge may degrade.
temporal_profile.recurrence: Maintenance, replenishment, retraining, recertification, inspection, and contingency exercises recur.
temporal_profile.censoring: Hidden labor, supplier risk, unsafe conditions, proprietary systems, and off-balance-sheet obligations may be missing.
temporal_profile.resolution: Resolve capability by exact action, resource, location, operator, dependency, time, and failure condition.

accumulation_profile.quantity_kind: Declared physical, financial, labor, time, data, and technical resource quantities
inflows: Funding, staffing, training, inventory, energy, access, data, equipment, maintenance, and redundancy.
outflows: Consumption, depreciation, turnover, outage, debt service, waste, access loss, depletion, and competing allocation.
decay_or_reset: Maintenance, replacement, retraining, replenishment, revalidation, decommissioning, or declared inventory reset.
accumulation_profile.scope: One bounded action envelope; only commensurable declared units may be summed, never capability, power, legitimacy, or readiness as a scalar.

observables: Resource quantities and units, ownership, conditions, operators, skills, dependencies, availability windows, tests, failures, maintenance, safety, lifecycle, exit, and repair capacity.

benefits: Pay, access, service, resilience, skill, and option value may accrue to different parties.
burdens: Labor, care, debt, extraction, energy use, maintenance, waste, surveillance, and risk may be externalized.
risks: Unsafe work, dependency, monopoly, depletion, ecological damage, technical lock-in, hidden fragility, and capability misuse.
voice_and_options: Record labor refusal, supplier alternatives, community objection, safety stop, accessibility, exit, decommissioning, and repair claims.
horizons: Acquisition, readiness, operation, maintenance, depletion, decommissioning, waste, debt, and ecological recovery differ.

distortions: Nominal budgets, vendor claims, inventory counts, technical demos, unpaid labor, hidden maintenance, supply risk, and narrow lifecycle boundaries can overstate capability.
counterflows: Resource refusal, reallocation, safe shutdown, redundancy, substitution, decommissioning, labor action, access revocation, and repair reserve.
failure_modes: Resources become capability, capability becomes authority, technical feasibility becomes safety, nominal capacity becomes available capacity, or capacity becomes predicted success.
repair_routes: Pause use, inspect dependencies, protect labor and affected parties, replenish or decommission safely, correct claims, resource repair, and reopen authorization.
repair_residuals: Debt, extraction, waste, injury, lock-in, lost skill, environmental damage, and dependency may remain.
repair_recurrence_checks: Review recurring shortage, hidden labor, maintenance deferral, vendor dependence, safety bypass, waste displacement, and unauthorized capability use.
evidence_requirements: Action-specific resources and units, owners, operators, access, dependencies, tests, limitations, time windows, safety, labor, lifecycle, failure, stop, and repair evidence.
alternative_paths: Use a less resource-intensive action, build redundancy, substitute a safer carrier, delay, narrow scope, use human review, decommission, or take non-action.
stop_conditions: Stop before attempt when authorization, operator safety, resources, maintenance, ecological limits, dependency, monitoring, stop route, or repair capacity is unresolved.
stall_or_block_conditions: Funding gap, labor refusal, outage, supply disruption, missing data, unsafe condition, expired credential, access loss, ecological constraint, or inadequate repair reserve.

recoverable_elements: Allocation, configuration, access, scheduling, inventory, and future operation may be changed or stopped.
residual_or_irreversible_elements: Extraction, emissions, waste, injury, debt, disclosure, sunk infrastructure, and lost options may persist.
prerequisites: Safe stop, decommissioning plan, labor and affected-party participation, resource ownership clarity, evidence preservation, and repair funding.

explicit_non_implications: Capability is not permission, authority, safety, action, effectiveness, resilience, legitimacy, or causal effect.

required_for: Acquiring, configuring, allocating, accessing, or invoking capability and protected resources for the proposed action.
non_implications: Possession, ownership, technical access, funding, or operator readiness does not grant authority or permission to use capability.

candidate_mediators: Which operator choices, configurations, dependencies, reliability conditions, implementation steps, and affected-party responses could connect capacity to action or outcome?
alternative_causes: Which independent resources, informal workarounds, external actors, shared infrastructure, or measurement conventions could explain apparent readiness or later events?
non_implications: Available resources or a successful test establishes no execution or causal effect.

stages.label: Attempt
stages.definition: A bounded invocation or repair attempt is witnessed with preflight, actor, proposal, authority reference, parameters, time, target or subject, capability context, and stop state without assuming execution or success.

carriers: Authenticated invocation, operator command, submission, transaction, physical initiation, dispatch, service request, or repair attempt record.
transformations: Parameter binding, authentication, scheduling, routing, preflight, validation, queueing, cancellation, retry, and failure handling.
gates: Current authorization, exact proposal and parameters, affected parties, rights and lawful basis, capability, preflight, safety, stop route, monitoring accountability, and repair readiness.

temporal_profile.onset: Authorization check, submission, queue entry, dispatch, and execution start may differ.
temporal_profile.duration: Attempt, queue, retry, timeout, cancellation, and observation windows are separate.
temporal_profile.latency: Network, administrative, physical, human, and dependency latency may obscure state.
temporal_profile.overlap: Retries, duplicate attempts, concurrent operators, prior actions, and external events may overlap.
temporal_profile.decay: Credentials, parameters, authorization, context, and target state may become stale before execution.
temporal_profile.recurrence: Retries and repeated attempts require idempotency, fresh gate checks, and separate records.
temporal_profile.censoring: Lost logs, private operators, disconnected systems, and destroyed records may hide attempts.
temporal_profile.resolution: Use unique attempt identity and event timestamps for preflight, dispatch, acknowledgement, cancellation, failure, and execution linkage.

inflows: Authenticated submissions, retries, repair attempts, and externally witnessed physical initiations.
outflows: Cancellation, timeout, rejection, failure, deduplication, expiry, or linked execution.
decay_or_reset: Idempotency reset, queue expiry, revoked authorization, changed target state, or new attempt identity.
accumulation_profile.scope: One action proposal, principal, target, parameter set, system boundary, and observation window; counts do not measure intent or effect.

observables: Attempt ID, actor, proposal, authority reference, subject or target, purpose, parameters, preflight, capability state, timestamp, acknowledgement, retry lineage, cancellation, failure, and execution link.

benefits: Service access, operator clarity, timely response, or remedy opportunity may be uneven.
burdens: Queueing, labor, monitoring, risk exposure, transaction cost, and repeated requests may be displaced.
risks: Duplicate invocation, unauthorized attempt, wrong target, stale parameters, unsafe retry, denial of service, and coercive pressure.
voice_and_options: Keep operator refusal, subject notice where required, cancellation, withdrawal, appeal, retry limits, and non-action visible.
horizons: Preflight, queue, dispatch, timeout, execution linkage, incident, retention, and repair horizons differ.

distortions: Duplicate IDs, missing clocks, retry collapse, optimistic acknowledgement, partial logs, actor ambiguity, stale authority, and wrong system boundary can misstate attempts.
counterflows: Cancellation, refusal, withdrawal, revocation, rate limit, queue removal, safe stop, rollback preparation, and documented non-action.
failure_modes: Attempt becomes execution, acknowledgement becomes completion, retry becomes persistence of authority, or failure becomes absence of impact.
repair_routes: Stop retries, revoke access, preserve logs, notify affected parties, correct target and parameters, contain partial effects, and reopen gates.
repair_residuals: Partial state changes, disclosure, resource consumption, queue displacement, fear, or external side effects may remain even without confirmed execution.
repair_recurrence_checks: Review duplicate attempts, stale authorization, unsafe retry, partial effects, operator override, missing logs, and repeated wrong-target invocation.
evidence_requirements: Unique attempt and proposal IDs, current gate references, actor, target, parameters, preflight, timestamps, acknowledgement semantics, retry lineage, failure, cancellation, and execution linkage.
alternative_paths: Cancel, defer, simulate without external effect, use manual review, route to a safer system, narrow scope, or take documented non-action.
stop_conditions: Stop or cancel when any current authority, target, rights, parameter, safety, capability, monitoring, or repair gate fails or becomes stale.
stall_or_block_conditions: Queue, rate limit, outage, refusal, invalid credentials, revoked authority, failed preflight, dependency loss, target mismatch, or unsafe condition.

recoverable_elements: Queued or not-yet-executed attempts may be cancelled and credentials or parameters changed.
residual_or_irreversible_elements: Disclosure, partial effects, resource use, queue displacement, external notification, and fear may persist.
prerequisites: Reliable attempt identity, cancellation path, evidence preservation, containment, affected-party notice, and fresh gates.

explicit_non_implications: An attempt is not execution, completion, success, effect, intent, persistence of authority, or permission to retry.

required_for: Submitting, retrying, routing, cancelling, or escalating an invocation against any external target or protected resource.
non_implications: Technical access, an accepted request, a prior grant, or a failed attempt does not authorize invocation or retry.

candidate_mediators: Which partial execution, notification, queue effect, resource use, operator response, or target-state change could connect an attempt to an outcome?
alternative_causes: Which concurrent invocations, external actors, system state, measurement loss, or background changes could explain the same outcome?
non_implications: Attempt timing, retries, acknowledgement, or failure status establishes no causal effect.

stages.label: Execution or action
stages.definition: A separately witnessed digital, administrative, embodied, material, or ecological action is linked to an authorized attempt and bounded target or subject without assuming success, intended outcome, legitimacy, or causal effect.

carriers: Operator act, service process, software execution, transaction, administrative change, communication, physical movement, material intervention, or witnessed non-action.
transformations: Input validation, actuation, transfer, modification, enforcement, communication, resource consumption, logging, containment, rollback, and termination.
gates: Live authorization, exact attempt linkage, target verification, preflight, monitoring, safety envelope, stop route, incident response, and repair readiness.

temporal_profile.onset: Start, first external effect, acknowledgement, and recorded execution time may differ.
temporal_profile.duration: Execution, exposure, persistence, containment, rollback, and observation windows are separate.
temporal_profile.latency: Actuation and downstream material or social response may be delayed.
temporal_profile.overlap: Concurrent actions, non-actions, dependencies, environmental events, and feedback may overlap.
temporal_profile.decay: Execution traces, target state, effects, credentials, and monitoring quality may decay or change.
temporal_profile.recurrence: Repeated, scheduled, iterative, or automated-seeming actions still require separate current authorization and records.
temporal_profile.censoring: Partial execution, silent failure, off-system effects, private operators, and missing logs may be hidden.
temporal_profile.resolution: Resolve start, partial state, completion status, termination, target change, and rollback as distinct events.

accumulation_profile.quantity_kind: Witnessed action events and declared material or digital changes
inflows: Separately witnessed executions, partial executions, resource transfers, state changes, and authorized repeats.
outflows: Rollback, reversal, decommissioning, expiration, recovery, or bounded state restoration.
decay_or_reset: Target reset, rollback, restoration, data expiry, physical decay, or declared observation reset.
accumulation_profile.scope: One action-attempt-target-purpose-system-time tuple; heterogeneous actions and social effects are not combined.

observables: Execution ID, linked attempt and proposal, actor, target or subject, start and end, status, state changes, resources, logs, monitor, stop events, failures, rollback, and external witnesses.

benefits: Service, transfer, protection, access, or material improvement must be observed by party and horizon.
burdens: Labor, compliance, extraction, surveillance, disruption, exclusion, risk, maintenance, and waste may be shifted.
risks: Wrong target, unauthorized scope, partial failure, coercion, safety incident, cascading dependency, irreversible change, and displaced harm.
voice_and_options: Maintain refusal, safe stop, withdrawal where meaningful, appeal, incident report, alternative service, exit, and remedy.
horizons: Execution, immediate effect, delayed effect, persistence, maintenance, reversal, repair, and future impact differ.

distortions: Success-coded status, partial logs, actor ambiguity, target mismatch, narrow boundary, missing non-users, hidden labor, and rollback claims can obscure actual action.
counterflows: Safe stop, refusal, withdrawal, containment, rollback, reversal, decommissioning, appeal, external intervention, and repair action.
failure_modes: Attempt becomes execution, execution becomes completion, completion becomes success, intended state becomes observed outcome, or actor log becomes causal proof.
repair_routes: Stop and contain, preserve evidence, notify and protect affected parties, reverse where possible, restore service, compensate, correct records, and reassess recurrence.
repair_residuals: Injury, exposure, dispossession, emissions, waste, distrust, fear, option loss, and third-party propagation may remain.
repair_recurrence_checks: Review repeated wrong-target action, authorization drift, monitoring gaps, partial failures, rollback failure, operator pressure, and displaced effects.
evidence_requirements: Unique execution and attempt links, current gate evidence, actor and target, timestamps, state witnesses, resources, status semantics, monitoring, stop events, failures, rollback, affected parties, and boundary limits.
alternative_paths: Stop, narrow, substitute a safer method, use staged human review, provide alternative service, restore prior state, decommission, or take documented non-action.
stop_conditions: Stop immediately when authority, target, rights, safety, monitoring, scope, capability, containment, or repair conditions fail or become unknown.
stall_or_block_conditions: Failed preflight, operator refusal, dependency outage, safety interlock, revoked authority, target change, resource loss, containment, or external stay.

recoverable_elements: Some digital state, transfers, access, configuration, service, or material conditions may be rolled back or restored.
residual_or_irreversible_elements: Bodily harm, disclosure, copying, emissions, ecological change, coercion, lost time, and social consequences may persist.
prerequisites: Immediate stop, reliable state history, backups or restitution resources, affected-party participation, fresh authority, and independent review.

explicit_non_implications: Execution is not success, intended outcome, causal effect, legitimacy, justice, consent, proportionality, or harmlessness.

required_for: Every external act, material change, communication, enforcement, transfer, data use, and repeat execution.
non_implications: A live system, operator instruction, prior attempt, decision, or capability record does not grant authority to execute.

candidate_mediators: Which delivered treatment, exposure, material pathway, institutional response, behavioral adaptation, or environmental process could connect execution to a declared outcome?
alternative_causes: Which concurrent actions, background trends, selection, anticipation, spillovers, shared shocks, or measurement changes could produce the observed outcome?
non_implications: Witnessed execution and temporal precedence establish no causal effect or attribution of an outcome.

stages.label: Outcome observation
stages.definition: A bounded digital, material, embodied, ecological, institutional, or public state is observed after or around an action under a declared construct, population, method, horizon, and missingness boundary without being called an effect.

carriers: Sensor, administrative record, survey, self-report, interview, audit, ledger, observation, ecological sample, complaint, service record, or affected-party account.
transformations: Construct definition, sampling, instrumentation, aggregation within valid units, linkage, coding, normalization, redaction, publication, and revision.
gates: Outcome definition, measurement validity, population and affected-party scope, privacy and rights, time window, missingness, baseline or comparator distinction, and review.

temporal_profile.onset: Action, possible effect, observation, measurement, and record time may differ.
temporal_profile.duration: State duration, observation window, instrument exposure, and record retention are separate.
temporal_profile.latency: Biological, material, institutional, ecological, reporting, and detection latency may be long or unknown.
temporal_profile.overlap: Concurrent actions, prior trends, adaptation, spillovers, seasonality, and external shocks may overlap.
temporal_profile.decay: Effects, states, biomarkers, memory, records, and instrument validity may decay differently.
temporal_profile.recurrence: Events, symptoms, complaints, service states, incidents, and measurements may recur.
temporal_profile.censoring: Loss to follow-up, privacy, refusal, death, migration, destruction, platform exit, and delayed reporting may censor outcomes.
temporal_profile.resolution: Declare construct, unit, population, place, horizon, event time, observation time, and record time separately.

accumulation_profile.quantity_kind: Declared outcome construct in valid physical, administrative, event, or instrument units
inflows: New measurements, events, affected-party accounts, corrections, linked records, and independently replicated observations.
outflows: Invalidation, deduplication, correction, reclassification, expiry, loss to follow-up, or deletion under lawful policy.
decay_or_reset: Instrument change, cohort reset, construct revision, baseline change, recovery, or declared observation-window closure.
accumulation_profile.scope: One construct-population-place-window-method definition; meaning, welfare, legitimacy, emotion, and heterogeneous units are not summed.

observables: Construct, unit, method, instrument, population, selection, baseline distinction, timestamps, missingness, privacy, affected parties, raw or referenced evidence, corrections, and negative cases.

benefits: Observed service, health, resource, access, safety, environmental, or option changes remain party- and horizon-specific.
burdens: Observed harm, exclusion, cost, labor, exposure, displacement, and maintenance remain disaggregated.
risks: Proxy error, missing non-users, surveillance, retraumatization, publication harm, aggregation bias, and boundary displacement.
voice_and_options: Preserve self-description, contestation, refusal, data correction, appeal, alternative measure, privacy, and nonparticipation.
horizons: Immediate, delayed, cumulative, recovery, recurrence, lifecycle, intergenerational, and ecological horizons remain separate.

distortions: Construct choice, proxy drift, attrition, survivor bias, underreporting, observer effect, selective publication, data linkage, and narrow boundary can alter the visible aftermath.
counterflows: Affected-party testimony, complaint, correction, independent audit, alternative measure, refusal, privacy protection, negative case, and boundary expansion.
failure_modes: Post-action state becomes causal effect, measured average becomes every party, absence becomes zero, intended target becomes complete boundary, or metric becomes value.
repair_routes: Protect parties, correct and version measurements, broaden boundary, restore missing voices, stop harmful data collection, preserve evidence, and open causal and normative review separately.
repair_residuals: Unmeasured harm, surveillance, retraumatization, stigma, missing records, ecological change, and delayed or irreversible effects may remain.
repair_recurrence_checks: Repeat measurement under declared horizons, inspect displaced and non-user effects, monitor recurrence, and audit whether prior missingness or proxy bias returns.
evidence_requirements: Declared outcome construct and unit, method, population, selection, instrument, timing, privacy, missingness, affected-party scope, corrections, negative cases, and system boundary.
alternative_paths: Background trend, common shock, selection, anticipation, substitution, displacement, concurrent action, measurement change, or natural recovery may produce the observation.
stop_conditions: Stop collection, linkage, publication, or downstream use when rights, privacy, safety, construct validity, missingness, boundary, or affected-party protection is inadequate.
stall_or_block_conditions: No opportunity, loss to follow-up, refusal, privacy restriction, inaccessible system, destroyed evidence, instrument failure, delayed detection, or unsafe reporting.

recoverable_elements: Current measurement, access, linkage, publication, construct, and corrective record may be changed.
residual_or_irreversible_elements: Underlying harm, lost evidence, prior surveillance, disclosure, stigma, bodily or ecological change, and delayed effects may persist.
prerequisites: Evidence preservation, privacy and safety safeguards, affected-party participation, independent review, and resources for longitudinal observation and repair.

explicit_non_implications: An outcome observation is not an effect, attribution, success, benefit, harm total, legitimacy, justice, emotion, or prediction.

required_for: Collecting, linking, retaining, publishing, interpreting for decisions, or acting on outcome data.
non_implications: A public event, operational log, research interest, or prior consent does not authorize every measurement, linkage, inference, publication, or reuse.

candidate_mediators: Which delivered intervention, uptake, exposure, material process, institutional response, or behavioral adaptation could connect action to this exact outcome construct?
alternative_causes: Which background trend, common cause, selection, anticipation, spillover, concurrent action, measurement change, or regression could explain it?
non_implications: Post-action timing, association, narrative fit, or observed change establishes no causal effect.

stages.label: Aftermath causal and normative assessment
stages.definition: Outcome observations, associations, a declared causal estimand and assessment, and separate rights or normative assessments are evaluated under explicit methods and frameworks without merging effect, legitimacy, goodness, or justice.

carriers: Outcome records, affected-party accounts, estimand specification, study design, causal assessment, rights analysis, ethical framework, distribution review, dissent, and uncertainty vector.
transformations: Construct definition, comparison, identification, modeling, sensitivity analysis, interpretation, rights reasoning, value articulation, distribution review, and publication.
gates: Outcome quality, estimand and comparator, assumptions, alternative causes, transport limits, affected-party completeness, named normative framework, jurisdiction, dissent, and review.

temporal_profile.onset: Outcome, detection, causal question, analysis, normative review, and publication may start at different times.
temporal_profile.duration: Effect windows, follow-up, assessment validity, rights impact, and repair horizons are distinct.
temporal_profile.latency: Delayed outcomes, reporting, identification, affected-party recognition, and institutional response may create long latency.
temporal_profile.overlap: Concurrent actions, feedback, adaptation, repair, shocks, and changing norms may overlap assessment.
temporal_profile.decay: Data quality, model fit, transportability, authority, and normative relevance may change over time.
temporal_profile.recurrence: Reanalysis, replication, rights review, appeal, reinterpretation, and updated aftermath assessment may recur.
temporal_profile.censoring: Missing outcomes, unpublished nulls, inaccessible data, unsafe testimony, lost parties, and truncated follow-up may censor assessment.
temporal_profile.resolution: Resolve outcome horizon, estimand, comparator, population, method, framework, affected party, and assessment date separately.

accumulation_profile.quantity_kind: Heterogeneous evidence, assessments, disagreement, and residual records
inflows: New outcome evidence, replications, counterevidence, affected-party accounts, causal analyses, rights findings, and normative arguments.
outflows: Retraction, invalidation, supersession, scope narrowing, data expiry, or explicit retirement of an assessment.
decay_or_reset: New evidence, method correction, changed conditions, framework revision, jurisdiction change, or declared fresh assessment.
accumulation_profile.scope: One estimand-population-horizon-method question and separately named normative frameworks; uncertainty and disagreement are not averaged.

observables: Outcome data, estimand, comparator, assumptions, identification strategy, sensitivity, uncertainty vector, alternative causes, transport limits, affected parties, rights analysis, framework, reasons, and dissent.

benefits: Effects and valued outcomes remain indexed by affected party, baseline, framework, and horizon.
burdens: Harms, costs, risk, uncertainty, lost options, and repair labor remain separate and cannot be netted away.
risks: Model overclaim, omitted parties, value laundering, average-effect dominance, transport failure, retrospective justification, and framework capture.
voice_and_options: Preserve affected-party interpretation, refusal, dissent, alternative estimand, rival model, competing framework, appeal, and unresolved disagreement.
horizons: Immediate, delayed, cumulative, recovery, recurrence, lifecycle, intergenerational, and ecological aftermath must remain separate.

distortions: P-hacking, model selection, construct drift, publication bias, framework laundering, aggregation, retrospective storytelling, stakeholder exclusion, and narrow boundaries can overstate closure.
counterflows: Replication, falsification, counterevidence, alternative estimand, rival model, affected-party testimony, rights challenge, dissenting framework, appeal, and non-action.
failure_modes: Association becomes effect, effect becomes success, average becomes everyone, effect becomes legitimacy, framework becomes universal truth, or absence becomes no harm.
repair_routes: Correct or retract claims, expand observation and party scope, preserve dissent, stop harmful use, provide remedy, reassess residuals, and require fresh authorization for any new action.
repair_residuals: Underlying harm, epistemic exclusion, stigma, prior decisions, lost trust, missing evidence, ecological change, and unresolved normative disagreement may remain.
repair_recurrence_checks: Repeat outcome review, test alternative causes, inspect transport and subgroup limits, track residuals, reopen rights analysis, and watch recurrence under fresh gates.
evidence_requirements: Quality-controlled outcomes, explicit estimand and comparator, identification assumptions, sensitivity and falsifiers, alternative causes, transport scope, uncertainty vector, affected parties, named frameworks, reasons, and dissent.
alternative_paths: No effect, heterogeneous effect, delayed effect, common cause, substitution, displacement, adaptation, measurement artifact, concurrent action, rival framework, or unresolved judgment must remain possible.
stop_conditions: Stop claim promotion or action when identification, measurement, affected-party scope, rights, framework, authority, transport, uncertainty, or falsifier requirements are inadequate.
stall_or_block_conditions: Missing comparator, confounding, weak measurement, censoring, unsafe testimony, inaccessible data, unresolved jurisdiction, affected-party omission, normative conflict, or inadequate follow-up.

recoverable_elements: Current claims, models, publications, decisions, frameworks, and data access may be corrected, narrowed, or retired.
residual_or_irreversible_elements: Underlying harms, prior reliance, stigma, exclusion, data exposure, lost opportunity, and ecological effects may persist.
prerequisites: Preserved evidence and history, independent review, affected-party participation, correction channels, fresh authority, and resourced remedy.

explicit_non_implications: Causal assessment is not legitimacy, goodness, justice, authority, prediction, or mandate; normative assessment is not causal effect or metaphysical verdict.

required_for: Collecting or linking evidence, publishing sensitive findings, making institutional decisions, or initiating any response or repair.
non_implications: Evidence quality, causal identification, affected-party support, moral argument, or urgent harm does not by itself grant jurisdiction or authority to act.

candidate_mediators: Which explicitly measured mechanisms connect the exact action contrast to the exact outcome under the declared population and horizon?
alternative_causes: Which confounders, selection processes, anticipation, interference, spillovers, concurrent actions, model choices, or measurement changes remain plausible?
non_implications: The atlas records requirements for causal assessment but performs no identification and asserts no effect.

stages.label: Feedback, challenge, and counterflow
stages.definition: Affected-party response, challenge, correction, counterstory, audit, refusal, withdrawal, appeal, and changed measurements may reopen any earlier stage without automatically commanding a new action.

carriers: Complaint, appeal, counterstory, correction, audit, whistleblowing, protest, refusal, withdrawal, incident report, affected-party account, replication, or changed measurement.
transformations: Attribution, triage, translation, aggregation within valid scope, verification, routing, protection, response, correction, escalation, and reopening.
gates: Safe access, non-retaliation, privacy, attribution, standing, response duty, independent review, preservation, urgency route, authority, and repair readiness.

temporal_profile.onset: Harm, awareness, expression, receipt, attribution, review, and institutional response may begin at different times.
temporal_profile.duration: Feedback availability, investigation, appeal, protection, response, and recurrence windows are separate.
temporal_profile.latency: Fear, power, access, detection, translation, queueing, and delayed effects may postpone feedback.
temporal_profile.overlap: Multiple complaints, counterstories, investigations, repairs, external events, and retaliation may overlap.
temporal_profile.decay: Evidence, memory, access, institutional attention, and protection may degrade while residuals persist.
temporal_profile.recurrence: Challenges, incidents, appeals, counterflows, and feedback loops may recur or reopen closed records.
temporal_profile.censoring: Retaliation, privacy, fear, inaccessibility, destruction, moderation, exclusion, and settlement may censor feedback.
temporal_profile.resolution: Resolve event, affected party, claim, recipient, response, protection, route, and outcome timestamps separately.

accumulation_profile.quantity_kind: Distinct feedback items, linked evidence, responses, residuals, and recurrence observations
inflows: Complaints, appeals, counterstories, corrections, audits, refusals, withdrawals, incidents, replications, and affected-party accounts.
outflows: Verified resolution state, withdrawal without adverse inference, correction, routing, deduplication, invalidation, or protected closure.
decay_or_reset: Fresh incident, new evidence, recurrence, changed affected-party scope, failed repair, or declared review reset.
accumulation_profile.scope: One issue taxonomy and review surface; item counts do not measure severity, legitimacy, trust, emotion, or consensus.

observables: Feedback artifact, attribution or protected anonymity, issue, linked stage or claim, evidence, affected parties, timestamps, route, protection, response, disagreement, correction, withdrawal, residual, and recurrence.

benefits: Voice, correction, protection, explanation, remedy access, institutional learning, and option restoration may be unequally available.
burdens: Proof, retelling, delay, translation, exposure, retaliation risk, appeal labor, and repair monitoring may fall on harmed parties.
risks: Retaliation, retraumatization, token consultation, surveillance, complaint laundering, capture, suppression, and premature closure.
voice_and_options: Preserve anonymity, refusal, representation limits, plural and conflicting accounts, appeal, escalation, exit, withdrawal, and non-action without adverse inference.

stall_or_block_conditions: Fear, retaliation, censorship, language or disability barrier, cost, queue, status, jurisdiction, missing records, inaccessible forum, capture, or unsafe disclosure.

residual_or_irreversible_elements: Harm, retaliation, disclosure, lost time, stigma, distrust, silenced accounts, and foreclosed opportunities may persist.

stages.label: Repair, review, and retirement

accumulation_profile.quantity_kind: Declared repair resources, obligations, events, outcome observations, residuals, and recurrence records
inflows: Protected evidence, repair proposals, funds, care, labor, corrections, restitution, compensation, rehabilitation, reforms, residual findings, and recurrence observations.

decay_or_reset: Fresh harm, recurrence, failed repair, changed party scope, new evidence, obligation expiry only where legitimate, or fresh review.
accumulation_profile.scope: One harm and affected-party set under named repair forms and horizons; pain, trust, justice, absolution, legitimacy, and residuals are not summed.

benefits: Safety, acknowledgment, correction, restitution, compensation, care, rehabilitation, option restoration, and non-repetition may matter differently by party.
burdens: Proof, retelling, waiting, care, monitoring, administration, funding, maintenance, and compromise burdens must be visible.
risks: Retraumatization, retaliation, coerced settlement, symbolic substitution, unequal remedy, premature closure, repeated harm, and displaced residual.
voice_and_options: Affected parties retain plural goals, refusal, privacy, representation limits, dissent, appeal, alternative repair, exit, and unresolved judgment.
horizons: Immediate safety, material restitution, care, recovery, institutional change, recurrence, intergenerational, and ecological repair remain separate.
